A route with no backing endpoints returns 503, not 404, so the headline advice cannot explain the symptom. It never checks whether Traefik accepted the route at all, which is the thing that actually produces a 404 for a route that exists.

I hold the pass because position in the answer changes the cost: 5a leads with that false cause and never mentions route matching, so it sends you to the wrong place. 5b leads with the match rule and demotes the false cause to a trailing aside.
